generatedProse.concept-context: In psychology, you meet experience in lab placements, research assistantships, and practical modules where you run studies or observe behaviour. Reflective practice means taking each of these through the cycle, not just recording that you did them. After a session observing participants, you look back honestly, link what you saw to theory you have met, and decide what you will do differently in the next study.
generatedProse.worked-example: Two psychology students complete the same research placement collecting observational data. One writes up a clear account of the procedure and the sample, and stops there. The other reflects honestly on a session where their coding drifted, links it to what they had read about inter-rater reliability, and sets out how they will tighten their protocol next time. Across the placement, the second student's reflective accounts show real insight, because reflection became a practice they repeated.
generatedProse.summary: In psychology, reflecting on experience becomes one continuing practice across your placements, practicals and research work. You run the cycle on each, reflect honestly, and articulate what you learned, so each study or observation feeds the next. It is the habit, not any single write-up, that turns your practical work into learning you can show.

check.body: A student finishes a placement, takes it through Kolb's cycle, reflects honestly on a session that went wrong, and writes an account showing what they now do differently. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved.
Nothing; feedback comes at the end, so it cannot affect anything that follows.
Only the mark on the first report, which cannot now change.
The deadline for the next report.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next report, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next report improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: That the three strands worked as one practice: the model, the reflection and the articulation together turned the placement into learning they can show.
_items.feedback: Yes. All three parts ran together on one experience, which is the whole practice.

_items.text: That only the parts of the placement that went wrong are worth reflecting on.
_items.feedback: Honest reflection covers what went well too, not only what went wrong.

_items.text: That the account is strong because it describes the placement in full detail.
_items.feedback: Description alone is not the point. The strength is the evidenced insight, not the detail of events.

_items.text: That the experience alone, once finished, counts as the learning.
_items.feedback: The experience is the occasion. The learning is what the student did with it through the practice.
